navigator.job: Own checkpoint intent, verified-only fresh resume, explicit compatibility, transactional migration, bounded installed-roster enumeration, green-main release sequencing, active-host root-entry ownership, unattended host boundaries, permissions, and final synthesis; verification receipts remain completion-runner-owned.

coach.job: Require, convert, and machine-link every reproducible nonpass verdict while keeping open evolution state bounded and rejected search knowledge queryable in a digest-bound archive.

gate.job: Independently compare candidates, shortlist current permitted cross-project evidence before full compatibility checks, fail closed on unresolved conflicts, separate exposed evaluation from one-shot holdouts, and promote, reject, or roll back.

product-builder.job: Implement the smallest complete product change, keep release-evidence vocabulary aligned with shipped contracts, remove measured avoidable work, and leave executable verification.

feedback.observed: An inspected project used both Codex and Claude Code but its Claude entry duplicated shared guidance while declaring the Codex entry canonical; the shipped contract did not deterministically preserve the inactive host entry during sequential adoption.
feedback.expected: Codex updates only AGENTS.md, Claude Code updates only CLAUDE.md, both reuse exactly one docs/nulnul live state, and switching hosts preserves the inactive entry byte-for-byte.
feedback.evidence: evals/host-entry-ownership/results.json records four sequential-order outcomes, eight controls, and one retired post-freeze mixed-host cycle without private paths or raw project content.

feedback.observed: Closed feedback, proposals, promotions, and autonomous episodes accumulated in the default evolution resume file until the current project state reached 164211 bytes.
feedback.expected: Ordinary resume loads only open work and current rollback points while complete accepted, rejected, rolled-back, and episode evidence remains integrity-checked and queryable.
feedback.evidence: The real state compaction regression preserved every full record, reduced active bytes from 164211 to 20560, was idempotent, and rejected archive digest and count tampering.

feedback.observed: The accepted-state contract required an already observed live cycle before a candidate could be activated, while public release evidence could match a version label without proving the exact candidate archive bytes.
feedback.expected: Keep the confirmed version active during a bounded provisional trial, confirm or roll back only after an observed cycle, and bind release credit to the exact plugin tree and distribution archive.
feedback.evidence: Schema-v4 lifecycle controls exercise pending, healthy, and breached trials; Release Gate negative controls reject a same-version different archive and stale public evidence.

feedback.observed: After exact-final evidence updated both README tables to the measured 239-test result, the locale-parity test still required the historical 234-test strings and failed one assertion.
feedback.expected: Keep the explicit English and Korean evidence-count guards synchronized with the measured full-suite count in the same release evidence change.
feedback.evidence: The focused locale-parity test rejected README.md only because '234 passed' was absent while the document truthfully reported 239/239.

feedback.observed: Three user-selected live projects exposed different forms of the same pre-execution gap: conflicting active instructions, a claimed but inactive guard with stale permissions, invalid resumable evolution history, and state that could not provide a safe rollback boundary.
feedback.expected: Before fast resume or implementation, classify each typed constraint once against current intent, derive every applicable, inactive, superseded, conflict, and unknown identifier mechanically, and fail closed when the review or its source inputs are stale.
feedback.evidence: The sanitized audit reproduced one contradictory platform ordering, one zero-hook configuration beside a claimed Stop guard and 51 retained allows, two active and 26 reconstructed live-cycle validation failures, one empty VCS metadata directory, and 25 unlinked triaged corrections. The prior prompt-only refinement then omitted required conflict identifiers in two of four runs.

feedback.observed: The derived-review candidate removed the champion's missing conflict identifiers, but the A/B output contract still asked the model to reassemble global decision fields after the deterministic writer ran. Candidate runs then changed permission_delta and handled an inactive guard inconsistently, scoring 0/4 despite the writer's deterministic negative controls passing.
feedback.expected: Evaluate and return the exact writer-produced decision: the model supplies only one relation per applicable constraint plus explicit non-permission supersessions, while the runtime derives every global field and distinguishes granted permission changes from merely required approval.
feedback.evidence: evals/constraint-reconciliation-v2/results.json records candidate 0/4 versus champion 0/4, complete candidate conflict identifiers, 1.42 percent paired input growth, four candidate activations, zero fixture writes, and no retained raw transcript.

feedback.observed: A live sequential Claude adoption appended the correct managed host block while preserving an older user-owned sentence that still declared the Codex entry canonical, leaving both root-entry authorities active at once.
feedback.expected: Before declaring host adoption complete, detect an explicit cross-host canonical declaration in the active root entry and require that active host to reconcile the exact line without mutating the inactive entry or shared state.
feedback.evidence: The live cycle preserved the inactive entry and four shared-state hashes, reproduced one conflicting legacy sentence after the shipped sync writer ran, and resolved it with one Claude-owned line edit while all shared-state hashes remained unchanged.
